A 30-year-old male arrives at the emergency department with acute abdominal pain. He reports
experiencing right lower abdominal discomfort throughout the day, accompanied by anorexia, nausea,
and vomiting. The pain intensified dramatically 30 minutes prior to arrival. His vital signs show:
temperature 102.5°F (38.5°C), blood pressure 105/79 mmHg, heart rate 148/min, and respiratory rate
17/min. Physical examination reveals rebound tenderness and guarding, with pain in the right lower
quadrant elicited during deep palpation of the left lower quadrant. What should be the immediate next
step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Diagnostic peritoneal lavage (B) Serial physical
examinations (C) CT scan (D) Immediate administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics (E) MRI of the
abdomen (F) Administration of analgesics and reassessment (G) Complete blood count and basic
metabolic panel (H) Laparoscopic surgery (I) Abdominal ultrasound (J) Observation for 24 hours

A. MRI of the abdomen
B. Observation for 24 hours
C. Serial physical examinations
D. Complete blood count and basic metabolic panel
E. Administration of analgesics and reassessment
F. Immediate administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics
G. Abdominal ultrasound
H. Diagnostic peritoneal lavage
I. CT scan
J. Laparoscopic surgery
